entities.summary:
Lucius Calpurnius Piso Caesoninus was a prominent Roman senator of the early Empire. Born in Rome around 55 BCE and died in 32 CE, he served as pontifex from 12 CE until his death. His tenure led him sometimes to be called Lucius Calpurnius Piso Pontifex, to differentiate him from his contemporary, Lucius Calpurnius Piso the Augur, consul in 1 BC.

Piso Caesoninus was a confidant of the emperors Augustus and Tiberius. He played a significant role in the governance of Rome during this period. Piso's relationship with these powerful Roman leaders is well-documented in historical records, making him an important figure to study for understanding the politics of ancient Rome.

Piso Caesoninus' legacy continues to be studied by historians today due to his prominent position in Roman history. His influence on Roman politics and governance makes him a crucial subject of research and analysis.

Lucius Calpurnius Piso Caesoninus was a pivotal figure in the early Roman Empire, whose impact can still be seen in the historical records of that era.
